# Part 1: Getting Started {background-color="#2C5F2D"}

## What is Quarto?

::: incremental
-   Write once → Export to HTML, PDF, Word
-   Mix text + code + output
-   Perfect for reports, papers, presentations
:::

::: fragment
**File extension:** `.qmd`
:::

## Your First Document

**Step 1:** Create new file `my-document.qmd`

**Step 2:** Add this at the top:

``` yaml
---
title: "My Analysis"
author: "Your Name"
format: html
---
```

**Step 3:** Add content below

**Step 4:** Render with `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K`

## Basic Markdown

``` markdown
# Main Heading
## Sub Heading

This is normal text. 

**Bold text** and *italic text*

- Bullet point
- Another point

1. Numbered item
2. Second item
```

## Adding R Code

Write code in chunks:

```` markdown
```{{r}}
# Load data
library(tidyverse)

# Calculate mean
mean(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
```
````

The code runs and shows output in your document!

# Part 2: Tables & Figures {background-color="#2C5F2D"}

## Making Tables

**Option 1: Markdown table**

``` markdown
| Name | Value |
|------|-------|
| A    | 10    |
| B    | 20    |
```

**Option 2: From R code** (better!)

```` markdown
```{{r}}
library(gt)

data %>%
  gt()
```
````

## Better Tables with GT

```` markdown
```{{r}}
Salaries %>%
  group_by(sex) %>%
  summarise(avg_salary = mean(salary)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_currency(columns = avg_salary)
```
````

::: fragment
Creates a beautiful, formatted table!
:::

## Regression Tables

```` markdown
```{{r}}
library(modelsummary)

model <- lm(salary ~ sex, data = Salaries)

modelsummary(model, stars = TRUE)
```
````

Shows coefficients, standard errors, and statistics automatically!

## Adding Captions

Add `#|` options at the top of chunk:

```` markdown
```{{r}}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Average Salaries"

Salaries %>%
  group_by(sex) %>%
  summarise(avg_salary = mean(salary)) %>%
  gt()
```
````

## Making Plots

```` markdown
```{{r}}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Salary vs Experience"

ggplot(Salaries, aes(x = yrs.service, y = salary)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal()
```
````

# Part 3: Equations & References {background-color="#2C5F2D"}

## Writing Equations

**Inline:** Use single `$`

``` markdown
The coefficient $\beta_1$ shows the effect.
```

**Display:** Use double `$$`

``` markdown
$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \epsilon
$$
```

## Numbered Equations

Add `\tag{}` for numbers:

``` markdown
$$
salary_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 sex_i + \epsilon_i \tag{1}
$$
```

Result: $$
salary_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 sex_i + \epsilon_i \tag{1}
$$

## Common Math Symbols

``` latex
$\alpha, \beta, \gamma$    # Greek letters
$x_i$                       # Subscript
$x^2$                       # Superscript
$\bar{x}$                   # Mean
$\hat{y}$                   # Predicted value
```

## Cross-References

**Reference tables:** `@tbl-name`

``` markdown
See @tbl-summary for results.
```

**Reference figures:** `@fig-name`

``` markdown
As shown in @fig-scatter...
```

**Reference sections:** `@sec-name`

``` markdown
# Methods {#sec-methods}

See @sec-methods for details.
```

# Part 4: Putting It Together {background-color="#2C5F2D"}

## Complete Document Structure

```` markdown
---
title: "My Analysis"
author: "Your Name"
format: html
---

# Introduction
Brief overview

# Methods
Describe your approach

# Results
```{{r}}
# Tables and figures here
```

# Conclusion
Summary of findings
````

## Useful Chunk Options

``` r
#| echo: false       # Hide code, show output
#| warning: false    # Hide warnings
#| message: false    # Hide messages
#| eval: false       # Don't run code
```

## Callout Boxes

Make important points stand out:

``` markdown
::: {.callout-note}
This is important information!
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
Here's a helpful tip.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
Be careful here!
:::
```

## Multiple Output Formats

Change YAML to export to different formats:

``` yaml
format:
  html:
    toc: true
  pdf:
    toc: true
  docx:
    toc: true
```

Now you can render to HTML, PDF, or Word!

## Common Issues

**Problem:** Code doesn't run

**Solution:** Check for typos, load required packages

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Problem:** Table doesn't show

**Solution:** Make sure you use `gt()` or similar

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Problem:** Reference doesn't work

**Solution:** Check label starts with `tbl-` or `fig-`

# Tips & Resources {background-color="#43464B"}

## Quick Tips

::: incremental
1.  Render often to catch errors early
2.  Use descriptive labels (`tbl-results`, not `tbl-1`)
3.  Always add captions to tables and figures
4.  Hide package loading messages with `#| message: false`
5.  Keep it simple at first!
:::

## Keyboard Shortcuts

**Render document:** `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K`

**Insert code chunk:** `Ctrl/Cmd + Alt + I`

**Run current chunk:** `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Enter`

# Quick Reference

## Minimal Document Template

```` markdown
---
title: "Title"
author: "Name"
format: html
---

# Introduction

Brief intro here.

# Analysis

```{{r}}
#| label: tbl-results
#| tbl-cap: "Results"

# Your code
```

See @tbl-results for findings.

# Conclusion

Summary here.
````

## Remember

::: incremental
-   **YAML** at top controls format
-   **\#** for headings
-   **Code chunks** between ```` ```{r} ```` and ```` ``` ````
-   **Labels** for cross-references
-   **Render** frequently!
:::

## Practice Makes Perfect

::: r-fit-text
Start simple,

add complexity

as you learn!
:::
